Thanks Neha — adding the CI/credentials detail here. Excerpt from ci-job-def.yml (annotated):

---
# Deploy-hotfix job (abridged)
steps:
  - name: mint-temp-creds
    run: |
      # uses vault auth role 'hotfix-deployer' to request token with TTL=300s
      vault token create -policy=hotfix-deploy -ttl=300s -orphan -format=json > /tmp/hotfix_token.json
  - name: use-temp-creds
    env:
      VAULT_TOKEN: $(cat /tmp/hotfix_token.json | jq -r .auth.client_token)
    run: |
      # deploy to canary using ephemeral token; no long lived secrets written to disk
      deploy.sh --env canary --token $VAULT_TOKEN

Audit controls: every token creation triggers an entry in Vault audit logs (immutable append only stream). We also record the CI job id and artifact digest in the release metadata JIRA-3421 (related_links).

Quoting our standard policy for emergency roles:
"Hotfix-deployer role can be assumed only when PagerDuty incident is in acknowledged state and an approved emergency PR exists. Tokens are issued with 300s TTL and are orphaned. CI deletes local temp files after use and the job emits an audit marker to the release ledger."

Let me know if you want the raw Vault audit lines for the deployment window; they are redacted for customer privacy in the shared Drive copy but we can provide a time‑boxed excerpt under an NDA.

—Irene

Adding the PR context and change notes. PR #8734 (https://git.redwood.ai/redwood/server/pull/8734) contains a one-line functional fix in handler.js and a CI gating change that wires in the hotfix-deployer role. Below is the PR description I used at the time: 

"Fix: prevent nil panic in request handler under rare race; backported to prod-stable. Triggered emergency deploy after observed errors in production. Verified on canary."

Approvals: Grace O'Connor approved in Slack + the PR approval. For the SIG evidence bundle we included the PR diff (pr-8734-diff.patch) and a timestamped screenshot of the Slack approval (in Drive).

Rollback plan (from runbook): if canary error rate exceeds 0.5% in first 30 minutes, revert PR, revoke any issued tokens (Vault revoke -prefix <token>) and run the hotfix rollback script. The runbook includes the revocation command sequence.

I can export a short greppable log of the deploy job (build id, job id, token creation line) if the assessor needs it.
